item.title: We learned 5 important things about the economy this week
item.description: From inflation, to credit card debt, to who's actually doing the spending: These are key takeaways from this week in economic news.
item.content:encoded:
From inflation, to credit card debt, to who's actually doing the spending: These are key takeaways from this week in economic news.

(Image credit: Sandy Guatibonza)
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: The money investors borrow to trade in the U.S. stock market is at an all-time high
item.description: Money that investors borrow to trade in the stock market is called margin debt. This debt is now above $1.5 trillion, 50% higher than a year ago. Could this spell trouble for the U.S. economy?

item.title: Latest inflation report may give the Fed more time for its control efforts
item.description: Inflation cooled a bit last month. Gas and grocery prices dipped and the overall cost of living rose more slowly, giving the Federal Reserve some breathing room for inflation control efforts.

item.title: How inflation is affecting consumer spending
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with Investopedia's Editor-in-Chief Caleb Silver about the impact of inflation on consumer spending.

item.title: People are giving up their pets due to costs — and rehoming them is more expensive too
item.description: The cost of pet care is rising. Petflation is affecting more than the cost of food and care; it's also making it costlier to transport pets between shelters, the key to getting many animals adopted.
item.content:encoded: The cost of pet care is rising. Petflation is affecting more than the cost of food and care; it's also making it costlier to transport pets between shelters, the key to getting many animals adopted.

item.title: Inflation eases in July as gasoline and grocery prices fall
item.description: Consumer prices in July were up 3.4% from a year ago — a smaller annual increase than in May or June. The news makes it less likely the Fed will feel the need to raise interest rates in September.

item.description: Shoppers' changing habits are fueling a major shift in what types of businesses are occupying storefronts.

item.title: Businesses feel the strain as the deadline for Trump's 50% Canadian tariff approaches
item.description: If President Trump's threatened 50% tariffs go through later this month, construction businesses that rely on materials imported from Canada are among those that will suffer.

item.title: Home sales fall in July amid high mortgage rates
item.description: The housing market is stuck in a slump. Sales of existing homes fell by 1.7% last month, even as the average selling price rose. High prices along with rising mortgage rates are putting a squeeze on affordability.

item.title: Inflation report to give new insight on the cost of living in America
item.description: The Labor Department releases a new report on inflation this week. It's higher than many would like, and with a sluggish job market, most people's paychecks aren't keeping pace with rising prices.
